title_guess: Human Development Index: development as quality of life, Mahbub ul Haq's four components (equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment), why measuring them is hard, HDI's three dimensions and the first Human Development Report
recurring_cast: measuring_tape icon (over 'economic growth', 'economic development' and later the human development panel)
crowd_people (one dark crowd icon reused for 'people', 'present generation', 'next generation', 'empowered people')

left sidebar checklist: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT - COMPONENTS with four rows (equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment); the current row is pulled out by a bracket line and a green tick_mark is added when a row is done
real_person_photo of Mahbub ul Haq with a national_flag, under the checklist
running_examples: no number example: each component is carried by one crowd picture (gold highlight for who benefits, two generations for sustainability, people -> output for productivity)
HDI = 3 dimensions: standard of living, health, education
first Human Development Report by UNDP, 1990, prepared under Mahbub ul Haq

best_moments.why: a gold circle lights a few heads in a dark crowd, tagged 'beneficiary of higher growth'; at 'benefit to every citizen' the gold spreads into an ellipse over the whole crowd: unequal vs equitable growth in one picture

the present-generation crowd sits inside a box of 'human development opportunities' with physical, financial and environmental chips; an arrow drops it to a next-generation crowd holding the same box and chips: sustainability as a hand-over between generations
four MEASURE lines leave the four components in a staircase, then a blue panel and a red DIFFICULT stamp fall over them: the measuring problem is shown before the index that answers it
HDI's three chips are wired back to the components list (equity to standard of living, productivity to health and education) while sustainability and empowerment stay unwired: what the index misses
the sidebar checklist ticks each component as it is finished and brackets the current one: a cheap, steady agenda tracker for a four-part list
the opening growth-vs-development split returns with HDI written where the question mark stood: the opening question visibly answered

weak_moments.why: a real photo of an economist with his national flag stays on screen for most of the video; BIE does not use photos of real people
productivity is only 'people -> economic output', with a 'productivity high -> high economic output' label and a sentence about skills and health; no picture of training, health care or rising output
empowerment, political democracy and economic liberalism are text labels with arrows and two callout boxes; no picture of people voting or choosing
a three-line paragraph restates the narration ('search for a comprehensive measure ... led to HDI') under the DIFFICULT panel

verify before reuse: the screen wires standard of living to equity, but income per head is an average and says nothing about how it is shared (an inequality-adjusted HDI exists for that); and the 'not captured' claim is shown only by missing lines, not marked
an equals sign 'economic development = human development' turns a simplification into a formula on screen
on-screen title grammar error ('what constitute development')

segments.teaches: recall: economic growth is measured by GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP and per capita income; economic development means quality of life, and how to measure it is the open question

elements.what: measuring tape icon over each side
ECONOMIC GROWTH (green) and ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT [quality of life] (blue), split by a dotted line
list under growth: GDP, GNP, NNP, NDP, per capita income
big hand-drawn question mark under development

segments.notes: 1 change event (the question mark at 12.6 s, on 'kis tarah se measure'). The rest is already built at 0 s (carried over from the previous video).
segments.idea: growth has well-known measures; development does not yet have one
segments.shown_as: two halves, each under a measuring tape: growth with its list of measures, development with only 'quality of life'; a big question mark drops under development as 'how can it be measured' is asked

segments.teaches: development reflects the quality of human life, so it can be called human development; which parameters count was an open question until Mahbub ul Haq named four essential components

elements.what: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT [quality of life] alone in the centre
a line drops from 'quality of life' to a small person icon labelled HUMAN; the person rises and '= HUMAN DEVELOPMENT' writes on
big red heading: what constitutes development?
pale yellow COMPONENTS box under 'human development', filling with the first item, equity
real photo of the economist with a national flag and his name strip, under the box

segments.notes: 5 change events. The four component names are spoken at 49-52 s but only 'equity' is clearly on screen by 49.7 s; the full list is in place when the next segment opens. Real photo: BIE must replace with a generic economist drawing or none.
segments.idea: development is about the quality of people's lives, and someone had to decide what that is made of
segments.shown_as: the development title zooms to the centre; a line drops to a small person icon marked HUMAN, which rises beside the title as '= human development'; a big red 'what constitutes development?' heading lands on top; a components box opens under 'human development' with the economist's photo below it and starts to list the parts

segments.teaches: equity: the benefit of growth usually reaches only a small share of people; equitable distribution is needed so that every citizen gains

elements.what: components list and photo slide into a grey left sidebar; equity row pulled out by a bracket line
dark crowd icon in the centre
gold circle over a few heads inside the crowd
pointer from the gold circle to 'beneficiary of higher economic growth'
three-line note under the crowd: equitable distribution is needed so growth reaches all sections
the gold circle widens into an ellipse covering the whole crowd

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 4 s). The gold highlight is on screen about 4.5 s before 'small percentage of people' is said; the widening lands on 'benefit ... har ek naagrik'. Reusable saancha: highlight a subset of a crowd, then grow the highlight to the whole crowd.
segments.idea: growth that lights up only a few people is not development; the light must spread to everyone
segments.shown_as: a dark crowd stands alone; a gold circle lights a small knot of heads inside it with a pointer 'beneficiary of higher growth'; a note on equitable distribution writes on below, and then the gold spreads into an ellipse over the whole crowd
segments.example: few heads lit -> whole crowd lit (no numbers)

segments.teaches: sustainability: the human development opportunities the present generation has (physical, financial, environmental) should pass as they are to the next generation

elements.what: green tick added to equity in the sidebar; sustainability row bracketed
crowd labelled PRESENT GENERATION
pale yellow box around the crowd titled 'human development opportunities'
three pale cyan chips at its side: physical, financial, environmental
down-arrow from the present crowd
second crowd labelled NEXT GENERATION, now inside the opportunities box with the same three chips

segments.notes: 6 change events (~every 4 s). Each chip lands on its spoken word; the box moves down to the next generation just after 'next generation' is said.
segments.idea: today's people must hand on their chances to tomorrow's people undiminished
segments.shown_as: a crowd marked 'present generation' gets a box of 'human development opportunities' with physical, financial and environmental chips; a down-arrow draws and the box and its chips move down to sit around a second crowd marked 'next generation', leaving the present crowd above

segments.teaches: productivity: a country's output is made by its people, so raising people's productivity through health, skills, education and food security raises output

elements.what: tick on sustainability; productivity row bracketed
crowd labelled PEOPLE
arrow from people to ECONOMIC OUTPUT
'PRODUCTIVITY HIGH' heading over a pale blue box around the people; 'HIGH' added before economic output
note under people: investing in skills, health etc. of our own people raises output

segments.notes: 5 change events. The cause is carried by labels ('productivity high' -> 'high economic output'); the four levers (health, skills, education, food security) are only in speech and a sentence.
segments.idea: more productive people make more output, and the government can make people more productive
segments.shown_as: a crowd labelled 'people' sends an arrow to 'economic output'; a 'productivity high' tag and a blue box wrap the crowd and the output becomes 'high economic output'; a note about investing in skills and health writes on underneath

segments.teaches: empowerment: people who can make decisions by their own will are empowered; this needs political democracy (choosing representatives) and economic liberalism (freedom from excessive economic controls)

elements.what: tick on productivity; empowerment row bracketed
crowd in a pale blue box labelled PEOPLE under the heading EMPOWER; box later grows and turns yellow
line under the box: empowering people to exercise their choice of their own will
'Political Democracy ->' and 'Economic Liberalism ->' pointing into the box
speech-box notes: people can influence decisions about their lives; people are free from excessive economic controls and regulations

segments.notes: 5 change events in 39 s (~every 8 s). The definition line appears about 1.6 s before 'apni marzi se' is said. Both inputs are text labels.
segments.idea: people are empowered when they can choose, politically and economically
segments.shown_as: under an EMPOWER heading a crowd box appears with a line about acting by one's own will; the box grows and turns yellow, then two labelled arrows, 'political democracy' and 'economic liberalism', point into it, each getting a speech-box note on what it means

segments.teaches: even with the four components defined, economists and bodies such as the UN, IMF and World Bank found it hard to measure and combine them into one index; continued effort produced the Human Development Index (HDI), which works on three dimensions: standard of living, health and education

elements.what: the sidebar becomes the main left panel: measuring tape icon, HUMAN DEVELOPMENT, four components all ticked, photo below
four lines, one from each component, each ending in the word MEASURE, stepped like a staircase
pale blue panel behind the four MEASURE lines
red rubber-stamp 'DIFFICULT' on the panel
three-line paragraph: the search for a comprehensive measure led to the HDI (term highlighted)
down-arrow from the paragraph to 'HDI'
'[3 dimensions]' chip, then three chips: standard of living, health, education

segments.notes: 9 change events (~every 5 s). The four MEASURE lines draw on 'kis tarah ... measure ... combine'; the DIFFICULT stamp lands about 1.8 s before 'difficult'. HDI and its chips land on their words.
segments.idea: four ideas are hard to fold into one number; the HDI does it with three measurable dimensions
segments.shown_as: the checklist, all four ticked, moves to the left under a measuring tape; one MEASURE line runs out from each component in a staircase, a blue panel slides behind them and a red DIFFICULT stamp thumps onto it; a paragraph writes on below, an arrow drops to 'HDI', which gets a '[3 dimensions]' chip and then standard of living, health and education chips

segments.teaches: the narrator maps HDI to the components: standard of living to equity, health and education to productivity; so HDI does not capture sustainability or empowerment

elements.what: MEASURE lines, panel and paragraph cleared; the HDI box with its three chips moves up beside the components list
line from equity to the standard of living chip
line from productivity to the health / education row

segments.notes: 2 change events; the productivity line appears between 219.7 and 229.7 s without its own event. Sustainability and empowerment are left without a line; nothing crosses or greys them while 'does not capture' is said. Verify the mapping before reuse (standard of living is an average income measure, not a measure of equity).
segments.idea: HDI covers only two of the four components
segments.shown_as: the clutter clears and the HDI box slides up beside the components list; a line draws from equity to standard of living on 'equity', and another from productivity to health and education, leaving sustainability and empowerment unconnected

segments.teaches: HDI was first introduced by UNDP in its first Human Development Report (HDR), published in 1990 and prepared under Mahbub ul Haq's leadership

elements.what: 'HDI' in magenta on a cleared canvas
UN emblem with the UNDP letter block and the programme's name
'published ->' arrow, later with 'Year 1990' above it
clipboard report holding 'HDI', labelled first human development report, with 'HDR' above
the economist's photo and flag under the report with a caption: prepared under his stewardship

segments.notes: 5 change events. The 'Year 1990' label has no separate event. Real emblem and photo: BIE should draw a generic UN-style agency building and a generic report.
segments.idea: a UN agency published HDI first, in the 1990 report
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to 'HDI'; the agency's emblem and name appear at left, a 'published' arrow runs to a clipboard report that holds HDI and is named the first human development report, 'HDR' writes above it, 'Year 1990' over the arrow, and the economist's photo with a stewardship caption drops under the report

segments.teaches: closing: the opening growth-vs-development split returns with HDI as development's measure; next video will show how HDI is calculated

elements.what: the two measuring tapes again
ECONOMIC GROWTH with its list of measures | ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT [quality of life]
'HDI' in magenta where the question mark stood

segments.notes: 1 change event. No recognised speech from 248.2 to 261.3 s (a long pause or lost words) while this picture is on screen; then the next-video teaser.
segments.idea: growth is measured by GDP and its family; development is measured by HDI
segments.shown_as: the opening two-column picture comes back unchanged except that a magenta 'HDI' now sits under economic development in place of the question mark

segments.teaches: channel end card (next video / playlist); not teaching
